title: Introduce failure-mode simulator for prompt-set regression contracts and CI integration
author: Priya Rao
description:
Context: As we extend our CI gates to catch subtle prompt-set regressions, we observed gaps where real-world failure modes (KV-cache eviction, truncated contexts, transient token drops, and backend latency spikes) do not appear in unit/eval tests and thus escape regression detection. Motivation: Build a lightweight, configurable simulator that can be run locally and in CI to inject realistic failure modes into prompt-set runs and assert metric-level contracts. This PR adds a Failure Mode Simulator (FMS) that can:
  - Inject context truncation (prefix/suffix drop) at configurable rates
  - Emulate partial KV cache eviction patterns and track resultant quality deltas
  - Simulate transient token loss/reordering to model transport/streaming artifacts
  - Produce burst latency profiles and delay token delivery to evaluate latency-sensitive rollouts
  - Produce a compact CSV/JSON report of per-prompt deltas and a synthesized "failure_contract" score used by CI gates

Design summary:
  - Language: Python module under eval-harness/src/sim to align with existing eval tooling.
  - API: CLI and programmatic runner (FailureModeRunner.run(config_path)).
  - Config: YAML contract describing failure types, seeds, intensity, and thresholds to assert (new contract field failure_contract_threshold).
  - CI: A GitHub Actions workflow that can be plugged into PR checks (runs a small sampled prompt-set under a tight failure profile and fails the gate if the failure_contract score exceeds threshold).
  - Metrics: Introduces a derived metric "failure_contract" which aggregates weighted metric regressions (e.g., accuracy/recall/semantic-sim) under injection. The weightings and fallback behavior are configurable per prompt-set.

Checklist:
  - [x] Simulator core implementation (token injection, truncation, latency profiles)
  - [x] Unit tests and property tests for determinism under seeds
  - [x] Small integration runbook and example configs under examples/
  - [x] GitHub Actions workflow and CI wrapper
  - [x] Docs describing when to add an FMS CI check to a prompt-set

Why this is different: Existing hooks catch drift and prompt-level regressions but assume normal serving conditions. FMS intentionally tests gating policy robustness under failure modes that frequently occur in production (e.g., partial cache eviction during autoscaling, ephemeral network blips for streaming responses). By surfacing the expected quality delta under injected faults, teams can pick conservative rollout policies and tune guardrails.

Testing and results:
  - Unit test coverage: 96% for sim module.
  - Locally ran the simulator against three representative prompt-sets (chat-help, summarization, search-rewrite). Under a moderate failure profile we saw the failure_contract score move from 0.03 -> 0.42 on the summarization set (CI threshold for that set set to 0.30; gate expected to fail).
  - CI: Workflow added as opt-in. In this PR the workflow ran on a small sample to validate speed (median run time: ~2m 18s). Initial CI run had a flaky integration test (timing sensitivity) which was fixed by adding a deterministic RNG seed argument.

Rollout plan:
  - Merge as opt-in tooling (default disabled for all prompt-sets).
  - Add example prompt-set contracts for two high-risk sets in a follow-up PR.
  - After two weeks of opt-in usage and stability, propose enabling for all release branches with conservative thresholds.

Open questions / future work:
  - Explore Rust/C++ hot paths for very large prompt-sets.
  - Add automatic suggestion for thresholds based on historical production deltas.
  - Add richer streaming reordering model for the JS/TS runtime.

review_comments: Kellen Brooks: Nice work — one concern: the default weights in failure_contract feel aggressive. Can we make the weight table explicit in the config and provide a conservative example?
Priya Rao (author): Agree — moved weights into the failure_contract.weights map and added conservative example in examples/ (see examples/failure-contract-conservative.yaml).
Marta Velasquez: The latency profile generator is helpful but stresses CI runtime. Please ensure the workflow uses a tiny sample and marks the job optional for non-critical PRs.
Priya Rao (author): Updated the workflow to run only on a 100-sample default and added an input flag for maintainers to increase sample size. Marked the action as optional in the doc.
Jason Liu: Add explicit RNG seed in tests so CI flakiness is reduced. Also add an integration test that asserts idempotency given the same seed.
Priya Rao (author): Added deterministic seed propagation and a property test — resolved.
Kellen Brooks: Approving pending a small docs tweak to clarify when teams should opt-in vs mandatory.
release_notes: Add Failure Mode Simulator (opt-in) for injected fault testing of prompt-sets; includes a GitHub Actions smoke workflow and docs. No behavioral changes to production code unless teams opt into CI check.
